solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shock with fool getting joint for daughter

indicators.note: 'getting joint for daughter' tells us one letter stands in place of another in the word for fool

parts.note: a dolt is a stupid person, a fool
J is an abbreviation for joint

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked when a foolish person turns up holding a cannabis joint in place of his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting ... for' swaps D (daughter) out of DOLT and puts J (joint) in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolt is a sudden shock, physical or emotional.

clue.text: Notice about old currency

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letter headings
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A notice is posted about money that is no longer legal tender.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to remark it, an older sense of observing.

clue.text: Leader of workers with time reportedly delivers pay restraint

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of 'workers'

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is to be heard rather than spelt, giving a word of matching sound

parts.note: to deliver someone is to free them, so delivers means frees

explanation.surface: A union boss with time on their hands announces limits on wages.
explanation.walkthrough: W from 'Leader of workers', AGE for time, then FREES (delivers) heard aloud gives FREEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage freeze is a government or employer policy holding pay at its current level, a form of pay restraint.

clue.text: Record of old with energy kept by the woman's assistant

indicators.note: a thing kept by another is held inside it, so these letters go within the pronoun

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
E is the physics symbol for energy
an LP, long-playing record, is an old-fashioned vinyl album

explanation.surface: A woman's assistant keeps an old vinyl album, full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept by' is the container signal; the energy letter goes before the record inside, against the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A helper is someone who aids another, an assistant.

clue.text: Musical producing a stir in confines of capital

indicators.note: in places the stir inside the boundary letters of the word capital
the confines of a word are its outer letters, here of 'capital'

parts.note: to rouse is to stir, wake up or excite

explanation.surface: A stage musical causes a commotion within the city limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confines of capital' gives C and L; 'in' puts A plus ROUSE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousel is a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical from 1945.

clue.text: Disturbance in fine American ship

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
USS, United States Ship, prefixes US Navy vessel names

explanation.surface: There is a disturbance aboard a fine American warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss is a commotion or disturbance, often over something trivial.

clue.text: One learning about origin of reform is more resolute

indicators.note: about means going around, so the learner's word wraps round the letter

parts.note: a studier is one who studies, one learning

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, here of 'reform'

explanation.surface: A student keen on reform is more determined than ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin of reform' gives R, which 'about' puts inside STUDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdier means firmer and more robust, so more resolute in purpose.

clue.text: Diets raved about and given publicity

indicators.note: about here means all around, in disorder, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Certain diets have been talked up enthusiastically and promoted in the media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of DIETS RAVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something advertised has been promoted publicly, given publicity.

clue.text: Staged work with some rare power on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection reverses an image, so the run is read backwards
some of the words means just part of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A theatrical production has a curious, uncommon strength on further thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes a run from RARE POWER and 'on reflection' turns it round: ARE PO read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music and staged in a theatre.

clue.text: English girl with posh date possibly given an assessment

parts.note: Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U usage

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: An English girl's smart date is being sized up by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles only the last word; 'posh' as U comes from the old U and non-U split of upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaluated means assessed, having had its worth judged.

clue.text: Time a prude is shaken up to buy a better property?

indicators.note: shaken up means jumbled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An era when a prim person is jolted into going upmarket in housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is shaken up' rearranges A PRUDE into RADEUP after T.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade up is to sell one thing and buy a better or bigger one, typically a house.

clue.text: Old bachelor with, say, ace comment

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
an ace in tennis is one kind of serve, 'say' marking the example

explanation.surface: An old single man joins in with a superb remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to remark or comment on something.

clue.text: Sign of agreement seen in a card game

indicators.note: something seen in another is placed inside it

parts.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
OK is a sign of agreement

explanation.surface: A nod of assent is spotted during a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container signal; 'a' meaning 'each', as in 'a pound a head', is the hard step.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a gambling card game of betting and bluffing.

clue.text: Fool besetting company meeting is beginning to misrepresent practical theory

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so the meeting goes within the fool

parts.note: a prat is a British slang word for a fool
AGM, annual general meeting, is a company's yearly meeting of shareholders

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of 'misrepresent'

explanation.surface: An idiot surrounded by an annual meeting starts to distort a down-to-earth philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'besetting' is the container signal and 'beginning to' takes one initial; PRAT is mild British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Pragmatism is the philosophy judging ideas by practical results, a theory of practicality.

clue.text: Spare type in service?

parts.note: read as a spare person attached to the armed services, held back to be called up when needed

explanation.definitionFit: A reservist is a member of a military reserve force, a spare soldier kept for call-up.

clue.text: Gear for don in a mess — feature of top flat?

indicators.note: in a mess means in disorder, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Equipment for a university teacher lies in a muddle, as seen in a penthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' rearranges GEAR FOR DON; a 'don' is a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden planted on a building's roof is a feature a top-floor flat might have.

clue.text: War alas felt more uncertain in novel

indicators.note: uncertain means unsettled, so the letters of the four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wartime feelings grow ever more doubtful in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' rearranges WAR ALAS FELT MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's 1929 book about the First World War is a novel.

clue.text: A revolutionary scientific place containing number getting jolly — that's irregular

indicators.note: containing means holding, so the reversed word wraps the next letters
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for the science room is read backwards

parts.note: a lab, laboratory, is where scientists work
NO is the abbreviation for number, from numero
a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A radical science lab with numbers and cheer: that's out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns only the lab, and 'containing' holds the number and the marine; 'jolly' for Royal Marine is old naval slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means deviating from the norm, irregular.

clue.text: Memorable uniform put on heads of the finest university lecturers

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: even means uniform, level and regular

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A notable occasion when uniforms are worn by top university teaching staff.
explanation.walkthrough: EVEN 'put on' T, F, U, L from 'heads of the finest university lecturers'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventful time is full of incidents, and so memorable.

clue.text: Rich source touring college getting by the sound of it suitable food item

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the source word goes around the letter

parts.note: a mine is a rich source, as in 'a mine of information'

indicators.note: signals a word that is heard the same as the one written

parts.note: meet is an old word for suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: A wealthy backer tours a college and is said to find a proper snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' is the container signal; 'by the sound of it' covers only the final piece. Mincemeat is a British dried-fruit filling for Christmas mince pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat, the spiced fruit mixture, is an item of food.

clue.text: One's also consuming dull part of salad?

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the word for also holds the word for dull

parts.note: too means also
mat, or matt, means dull, without shine

explanation.surface: Something also eats a lacklustre ingredient of a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' is the container signal. 'One's' plays no part in the wordplay and only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomato is a common salad ingredient; the question mark admits it is only one example.

clue.text: Good animals on way back showing rapacity

indicators.note: on the way back means going in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: deer are animals

explanation.surface: Grazing beasts heading home show their hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way back' turns only the animals, which then read as a water plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is an excessive desire for more, rapacity.

clue.text: Organised group of workers left in European yard

indicators.note: in places the word for left inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: to quit is to leave, so quit means left

explanation.surface: A trade union walked out from a European yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts QUIT between E and Y. EQUITY is the British actors' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the actors' trade union in Britain, an organised body of workers.

clue.text: Stream from old river flanked by another

indicators.note: flanked by means having something on each side, so the letters sit inside the other river

parts.note: another river, the Trent, a major river in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A flow of water comes from an ancient river bordered by a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flanked by' puts O and R inside TRENT, the English river 'another' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a fast, violent stream of water.

clue.text: River cruise initially for powerful business figure

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of 'cruise' is taken

explanation.surface: A river cruise is laid on for a top company boss.
explanation.walkthrough: EXE, the Devon river, then C from 'cruise initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exec, short for executive, is a senior business figure.

clue.text: Brand of car close to notable entertainment venue?

parts.note: a marque is a make or brand, especially of car

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, here of 'notable'

explanation.surface: A car maker's name appears near a prominent entertainment spot.
explanation.walkthrough: MARQUE plus E from 'close to notable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties and shows, so a temporary venue for entertainment.

clue.text: Prophet is last character found in long period

indicators.note: one thing found in another is inside it

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
Z is the last character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A seer's final role is uncovered in an age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts Z inside ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is a Hebrew scribe and prophet with a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Outfit for distant travel in resort with clubs, say, fringing church

indicators.note: fringing means bordering on both sides, so the two words go around the church letters

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
clubs is one suit of cards, 'say' marking the example
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A holiday resort with golf clubs surrounding a church is a far-flung trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringing' has the resort and the card suit on either side of the church; 'say' marks clubs as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacesuit is the pressurised outfit astronauts wear for travel beyond Earth.

clue.text: Festival son ignored getting apple?

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so the letter is dropped from the festival

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: A son missing the holiday ends up with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' drops S from EASTER. An eating apple, unlike a cooker, is called an eater.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is an apple grown for eating raw, a dessert apple rather than a cooker.
